# Shared ontology

<!-- Generated by bin/ontology.py --write. Edit catalog/ontology.json, not this page. -->

Ontology version: **1.0.0**. Canonical registry SHA-256: `071bc05833f322e4aa8d43791fdc536a8746fe0187333b4dc7aab3e19b30d403`.

The versioned registry defines the shared vocabulary. This page is its generated, on-demand reference; it is not globally injected resident context.

## Use and authority

Structured semantic references must use exact canonical IDs. Aliases require an explicit migration choice; the validator never silently rewrites them. Existing field names can retain a checked binding while their owning contract is migrated.

A binding checks its canonical term reference, field presence and JSON type. It does not prove that the chosen meaning is correct or that a program implements the definition. Relationships describe the model; they are not executable permission rules, a reasoner or authorization evidence. Owners identify maintenance responsibility, not permission to authorize an operation.

The validator seals relationships involving `authorization-record`, `authorization-scope` or any term maintained by the `authority` owner. The only permitted signature is `authorization-record binds authorization-scope`, and that relationship and its two terms are required. All other incoming or outgoing edges fail regardless of the verb, including configuration or skill replacement creating authorization. Changing an owner cannot unprotect the two canonical terms or qualify a new subject. Adding a relationship at this boundary requires a reviewed change to the explicit allowlist in `bin/ontology.py`; non-authority relationships remain extensible. This is a structural vocabulary constraint, not proof about arbitrary prose or runtime authorization.

Configuration, artifact checks, runtime observation and protected acceptance are separate claims. Always name the target, revision, boundary and evidence relevant to a claim. A skill replacement, label or configured flag cannot manufacture authorization or live enforcement.

## Canonical terms

<a id="acceptance-blocking"></a>
### Acceptance blocking

ID: `acceptance-blocking` · Owner: `verification` · Work: #1002, #1003

Observed protection at a declared acceptance boundary actually prevents an invalid candidate from being accepted, with exact candidate/range and protection configuration bound to the evidence.

- Example: Protected checks reject a candidate containing an invalid commit even when local hooks were bypassed.
- Distinguish from: [configured](#configured), [installed](#installed), [runtime-observed](#runtime-observed).

<a id="activation-receipt"></a>
### Activation receipt

ID: `activation-receipt` · Owner: `packaging` · Work: #1000, #851

A record of the coherent artifact and policy set actually activated, its validation evidence and prior compatible state; it is not new authorization.

- Example: Activation records the new parent lock and policy digest plus the prior rollback target.
- Distinguish from: [rollback-receipt](#rollback-receipt), [authorization-record](#authorization-record), [generated-artifact](#generated-artifact).

<a id="applicability-scope"></a>
### Applicability scope

ID: `applicability-scope` · Owner: `policy` · Work: #848, #1002

The targets and operation classes for which a policy, skill or check is relevant.

- Example: A notebook check applies only to the declared project and notebook changes.
- Distinguish from: [repository-identity](#repository-identity), [authorization-scope](#authorization-scope).

<a id="artifact-verified"></a>
### Artifact verified

ID: `artifact-verified` · Owner: `verification` · Work: #1004, #847

An identified artifact set passed declared provenance, content and compatibility checks; this is a scoped artifact claim.

- Example: Installed file hashes match the approved package and project composition.
- Distinguish from: [configuration-valid](#configuration-valid), [runtime-observed](#runtime-observed), [acceptance-blocking](#acceptance-blocking).

<a id="authorization-record"></a>
### Authorization record

ID: `authorization-record` · Owner: `authority` · Work: #848, #1002

A record of permission or an approved scoped exception from an authorized issuer, with scope and validity; the record cannot create its own issuer authority. A project-scoped exception cannot extend to another project or weaken the common integrity floor.

- Example: An approved exception identifies its issuer, allowed operation and expiration.
- Distinguish from: [evidence](#evidence), [policy-override](#policy-override), [skill-replacement](#skill-replacement).

<a id="authorization-scope"></a>
### Authorization scope

ID: `authorization-scope` · Owner: `authority` · Work: #848, #1002

The actors, resources, operations and validity limits covered by an actual authorization.

- Example: Permission to inspect one repository does not grant deployment authority.
- Distinguish from: [applicability-scope](#applicability-scope), [repository-identity](#repository-identity).

<a id="common-integrity-floor"></a>
### Common integrity floor

ID: `common-integrity-floor` · Owner: `policy` · Work: #1000, #851

Shared requirements for authorization, credential handling, work preservation and evidence integrity; selected workflow topology is defined separately in profiles.

- Example: Replacing a project workflow does not waive credential handling or invent approval.
- Distinguish from: [profile](#profile), [policy-override](#policy-override).

<a id="configuration-valid"></a>
### Configuration valid

ID: `configuration-valid` · Owner: `verification` · Work: #851, #848

A named configuration passed its declared structural and consistency checks at an exact revision.

- Example: A schema check rejects unknown fields and accepts the two valid profile fixtures.
- Distinguish from: [artifact-verified](#artifact-verified), [runtime-observed](#runtime-observed), [acceptance-blocking](#acceptance-blocking).

<a id="configured"></a>
### Configured

ID: `configured` · Owner: `verification` · Work: #1003, #851

A declared setting or registration exists for an identified target; this fact alone says nothing about artifact presence or observed behavior.

- Example: Settings name a hook command that has not yet been installed or observed.
- Distinguish from: [installed](#installed), [runtime-observed](#runtime-observed), [acceptance-blocking](#acceptance-blocking).

<a id="effective-policy"></a>
### Effective policy

ID: `effective-policy` · Owner: `policy` · Work: #848, #1002

The deterministic result of resolving approved parent, organization and project policy inputs, with provenance and a revision or digest. Evaluate a policy-changing operation under the previously approved policy, not its proposed replacement.

- Example: An explanation reports the controlling ticket syntax and its approved source.
- Distinguish from: [policy-override](#policy-override), [evidence](#evidence).

<a id="evidence"></a>
### Evidence

ID: `evidence` · Owner: `verification` · Work: #1002, #1003

An observable record supporting a specific claim, bound to relevant source, target, revision, method and validity conditions.

- Example: A canary records the exact adapter revision and the prevented side effect.
- Distinguish from: [authorization-record](#authorization-record), [configured](#configured).

<a id="gate"></a>
### Gate

ID: `gate` · Owner: `enforcement` · Work: #851, #1002

A check that evaluates operation facts and evidence against applicable policy at a declared boundary and returns a decision.

- Example: A ticket gate inspects actual commit messages in the candidate range.
- Distinguish from: [host-adapter](#host-adapter), [acceptance-blocking](#acceptance-blocking).

<a id="generated"></a>
### Generated

ID: `generated` · Owner: `packaging` · Work: #1004, #851

An artifact was produced from identified inputs; generation alone does not establish installation, runtime execution or acceptance protection.

- Example: A build emits a hook manifest into its output tree.
- Distinguish from: [installed](#installed), [artifact-verified](#artifact-verified).

<a id="generated-artifact"></a>
### Generated artifact

ID: `generated-artifact` · Owner: `packaging` · Work: #1000, #851

Output derived from identified source inputs and a generator version; provenance and verification are separate recorded properties.

- Example: A generated resident file records the parent and project inputs used to compose it.
- Distinguish from: [effective-policy](#effective-policy), [activation-receipt](#activation-receipt).

<a id="host-adapter"></a>
### Host adapter

ID: `host-adapter` · Owner: `host-adapter` · Work: #1003, #851

The implementation that maps structured inputs and decisions to a particular host protocol and observes its outcome.

- Example: An adapter translates a denial into the supported tool-interception response.
- Distinguish from: [host-capability](#host-capability), [policy](#policy).

<a id="host-capability"></a>
### Host capability

ID: `host-capability` · Owner: `host-adapter` · Work: #1003, #851

A specific mechanism a pinned host/backend combination can provide, with capability evidence recorded separately from configuration.

- Example: Tool-call denial and instruction delivery are separate host capabilities.
- Distinguish from: [procedure-binding](#procedure-binding), [configured](#configured), [acceptance-blocking](#acceptance-blocking).

<a id="installed"></a>
### Installed

ID: `installed` · Owner: `packaging` · Work: #1003, #1004

Identified artifacts are present at the intended consumer locations; installation alone does not prove the host executes them.

- Example: A hook file is present at its configured path.
- Distinguish from: [configured](#configured), [runtime-observed](#runtime-observed), [acceptance-blocking](#acceptance-blocking).

<a id="local-feedback"></a>
### Local feedback

ID: `local-feedback` · Owner: `enforcement` · Work: #1000, #851

A locally executed check or diagnostic that may prevent a normal local operation but can be bypassed outside its declared local boundary.

- Example: A native commit hook rejects a missing ticket; bypassing that hook remains possible.
- Distinguish from: [acceptance-blocking](#acceptance-blocking).

<a id="parent-lock"></a>
### Parent lock

ID: `parent-lock` · Owner: `packaging` · Work: #851, #1004

An immutable reference to the approved parent source and compatible artifacts, including revision and provenance needed to detect mixed inputs.

- Example: Skills and runtime artifacts identify the same parent commit and compatible build.
- Distinguish from: [profile](#profile), [rollback-receipt](#rollback-receipt), [source-reference](#source-reference).

<a id="parent-scaffold"></a>
### Parent scaffold

ID: `parent-scaffold` · Owner: `scaffolding` · Work: #851, #848

Reusable definitions, composition and verification mechanisms shared by consumers; selected organization or project workflow choices live in profiles.

- Example: One parent package serves strict-release and synthetic-trunk.
- Distinguish from: [profile](#profile).

<a id="policy"></a>
### Policy

ID: `policy` · Owner: `policy` · Work: #848, #851

Approved criteria governing an operation, including permitted configuration and required evidence; policy does not grant platform permissions.

- Example: The selected policy requires a ticket identifier on accepted commits.
- Distinguish from: [skill](#skill), [authorization-record](#authorization-record).

<a id="policy-override"></a>
### Policy override

ID: `policy-override` · Owner: `policy` · Work: #848, #851

An explicit change to a policy field that the controlling approved layer permits a lower layer to customize.

- Example: A permitted project setting chooses a different ticket syntax.
- Distinguish from: [skill-replacement](#skill-replacement), [resident-composition](#resident-composition), [authorization-record](#authorization-record).

<a id="procedure-binding"></a>
### Procedure binding

ID: `procedure-binding` · Owner: `composition` · Work: #1001, #851

An explicit association between a task procedure role and the qualified skill selected to perform it.

- Example: The review role selects a project-specific review skill.
- Distinguish from: [host-capability](#host-capability), [skill-replacement](#skill-replacement).

<a id="profile"></a>
### Profile

ID: `profile` · Owner: `policy` · Work: #848, #1002

An approved named set of workflow policy values and permitted project customizations selected for a declared scope.

- Example: One profile targets develop; another permits feature branches to target main.
- Distinguish from: [parent-scaffold](#parent-scaffold), [policy-override](#policy-override).

<a id="project"></a>
### Project

ID: `project` · Owner: `policy` · Work: #848, #1001

A declared consumer scope with canonical repository identities, a selected profile and explicit composition inputs.

- Example: A project declares its repository and binds a project review procedure.
- Distinguish from: [repository-identity](#repository-identity).

<a id="repository-identity"></a>
### Repository identity

ID: `repository-identity` · Owner: `policy` · Work: #848, #1002

Canonical host, owner and repository identifiers used to identify the actual operation target repository. Directory or file applicability is a separate scope bound to that identity. Missing, foreign or ambiguous identity remains unknown and cannot inherit a neighboring project.

- Example: Equal repository basenames under different owners do not identify the same target.
- Distinguish from: [applicability-scope](#applicability-scope), [authorization-scope](#authorization-scope).

<a id="resident-block"></a>
### Resident block

ID: `resident-block` · Owner: `composition` · Work: #1001, #1003

A stable identified section of instructions selected to remain in the active resident context.

- Example: A workflow block carries the selected project topology.
- Distinguish from: [skill](#skill).

<a id="resident-composition"></a>
### Resident composition

ID: `resident-composition` · Owner: `composition` · Work: #1001, #1004

Deterministic assembly of parent and project resident blocks using declared replacement or extension, provenance and a final size budget. Every managed output must identify the same approved parent lock; mixed parent inputs are invalid.

- Example: A project replaces its workflow block and preserves common integrity blocks.
- Distinguish from: [policy-override](#policy-override), [skill-replacement](#skill-replacement).

<a id="rollback-receipt"></a>
### Rollback receipt

ID: `rollback-receipt` · Owner: `packaging` · Work: #1004, #1005

A record identifying the exact previous compatible artifact and policy set and the state compatibility needed to restore it. The target is a previously approved exact lock and effective-policy digest, never a live branch or tag tip.

- Example: Rollback names the prior immutable set and invalidates incompatible task evidence.
- Distinguish from: [parent-lock](#parent-lock), [authorization-record](#authorization-record).

<a id="runtime-observed"></a>
### Runtime observed

ID: `runtime-observed` · Owner: `verification` · Work: #1003, #1002

The declared behavior was actually exercised through the identified registered path in a pinned runtime, with the outcome recorded.

- Example: An allowed operation succeeds and a denial canary leaves its target unchanged.
- Distinguish from: [installed](#installed), [acceptance-blocking](#acceptance-blocking).

<a id="skill"></a>
### Skill

ID: `skill` · Owner: `composition` · Work: #1001, #848

A scoped procedure or reference resource selected for a task; reading or replacing its prose cannot create permission or approval.

- Example: A code review skill supplies a review procedure.
- Distinguish from: [policy](#policy), [host-capability](#host-capability).

<a id="skill-extension"></a>
### Skill extension

ID: `skill-extension` · Owner: `composition` · Work: #1001, #848

An explicit composition declaration adding scoped skill content in a declared order while retaining the referenced base procedure.

- Example: A project review adds a notebook check after the general review.
- Distinguish from: [skill-replacement](#skill-replacement).

<a id="skill-replacement"></a>
### Skill replacement

ID: `skill-replacement` · Owner: `composition` · Work: #1001, #848

An explicit composition declaration selecting a qualified skill instead of another for the declared procedure role and scope.

- Example: The default review procedure is replaced across explicit and prerequisite routes.
- Distinguish from: [policy-override](#policy-override), [skill-extension](#skill-extension), [authorization-record](#authorization-record).

<a id="source-reference"></a>
### Source reference

ID: `source-reference` · Owner: `packaging` · Work: #1000, #851

A repository locator and revision expression; a branch or tag name alone is mutable and does not establish an immutable parent lock.

- Example: Resolve a branch to its exact approved commit before generating or activating artifacts.
- Distinguish from: [parent-lock](#parent-lock).

## Relationships

- `adapter-implements-capability`: [host-adapter](#host-adapter) **implements** [host-capability](#host-capability). Implementation presence does not establish observed capability.
- `artifact-identifies-parent`: [generated-artifact](#generated-artifact) **identifies** [parent-lock](#parent-lock). Composed managed artifacts must identify one compatible immutable parent; a mixed-lock result is invalid.
- `authorization-binds-scope`: [authorization-record](#authorization-record) **binds** [authorization-scope](#authorization-scope). The issuer authority and scope are established outside this registry.
- `binding-selects-skill`: [procedure-binding](#procedure-binding) **selects** [skill](#skill). Selecting a procedure does not grant authorization.
- `composition-assembles-blocks`: [resident-composition](#resident-composition) **assembles** [resident-block](#resident-block). The final composed context is measured and scoped.
- `evidence-supports-acceptance-claim`: [evidence](#evidence) **supports** [acceptance-blocking](#acceptance-blocking). A passing schema or an installed hook alone cannot support this claim.
- `evidence-supports-runtime-claim`: [evidence](#evidence) **supports** [runtime-observed](#runtime-observed). A runtime claim needs evidence from the actual registered path.
- `extension-adds-skill`: [skill-extension](#skill-extension) **adds** [skill](#skill). The declared order retains the base procedure.
- `gate-evaluates-policy`: [gate](#gate) **evaluates** [effective-policy](#effective-policy). The gate uses operation facts and separately supplied evidence.
- `policy-preserves-common-floor`: [effective-policy](#effective-policy) **preserves** [common-integrity-floor](#common-integrity-floor). Authorized workflow configuration cannot weaken the shared integrity requirements.
- `profile-configures-policy`: [profile](#profile) **configures** [policy](#policy). Only approved values and permitted overrides participate.
- `project-selects-profile`: [project](#project) **selects** [profile](#profile). Selection is scoped to the declared project identity.
- `replacement-selects-skill`: [skill-replacement](#skill-replacement) **selects** [skill](#skill). The explicit replacement applies to every declared loading route.
- `rollback-identifies-parent`: [rollback-receipt](#rollback-receipt) **identifies** [parent-lock](#parent-lock). Rollback identifies an exact compatible set rather than a moving branch tip.

## Ambiguous and former names

These spellings are rejected as machine term references. The prose linter only advises; context determines the intended replacement.

- `capability` (ambiguous): `host-capability`, `procedure-binding`.
- `enforcement-live` (deprecated): `acceptance-blocking`.
- `native-shadow` (deprecated): `skill-replacement`.
- `override` (ambiguous): `policy-override`, `skill-replacement`, `skill-extension`, `resident-composition`.
- `scope` (ambiguous): `repository-identity`, `applicability-scope`, `authorization-scope`.
- `verified` (ambiguous): `configuration-valid`, `artifact-verified`, `runtime-observed`, `acceptance-blocking`.

## Checked artifact bindings

These bindings annotate existing fields without changing their runtime schema. In particular, a legacy `blocking` boolean describes configuration, not observed protected acceptance.

- `catalog/resolver-manifest.json`:
  - `/projects/*/repos/*` → `repository-identity` (string).
  - `/routes/*/skills/*` → `skill` (string).
  - `/projects/*/routes/*/skills/*` → `skill` (string).
- `dist/craft-agent/enforcement-manifest.json`:
  - `/gates/*` → `gate` (object).
  - `/gates/*/runtime_policy/*` → `configured` (string).
  - `/gates/*/blocking` → `configured` (boolean).
  - `/gate_contract` → `generated-artifact` (object).
  - `/effective_policy` → `generated-artifact` (object).
  - `/effective_policy_evidence_state` → `configured` (string).
- `catalog/effective-policy.json`:
  - `/organization_profiles/*` → `profile` (object).
  - `/projects/*` → `project` (object).
  - `/projects/*/repository_identity` → `repository-identity` (object).
  - `/organization_profiles/1/values/branch-policy` → `policy-override` (object).
  - `/projects/1/values/review-procedure-binding` → `policy-override` (object).
  - `/parent_contract_revision` → `source-reference` (string).
  - `/parent_lock` → `parent-lock` (object).
- `catalog/gate-contracts.json`:
  - `/policy_fields/0` → `policy` (object).
  - `/policy_fields/1` → `policy` (object).
  - `/policy_fields/2` → `procedure-binding` (object).
  - `/policy_fields/*/override_policy` → `policy-override` (object).
  - `/policy_fields/*/required_capability_ids/*` → `host-capability` (string).
  - `/capabilities/*` → `host-capability` (object).
  - `/capabilities/*/configured_evidence_only` → `configured` (boolean).
- `examples/scaffolding/strict-release-policy.json`:
  - `/repository_identity` → `repository-identity` (object).
  - `/parent_lock` → `parent-lock` (object).
  - `/values/review-procedure-binding` → `procedure-binding` (object).
- `examples/scaffolding/synthetic-trunk-policy.json`:
  - `/repository_identity` → `repository-identity` (object).
  - `/parent_lock` → `parent-lock` (object).
  - `/values/review-procedure-binding` → `procedure-binding` (object).

## Consumer compatibility

Synthetic consumer A preserves parent-owned content and adds a declared project layer. Synthetic consumer B imports an explicit legacy native-shadow declaration as a skill replacement. Both use the same parent definitions and explicit resident composition; neither makes its local workflow a universal default.

An ambiguous local term needs a scoped mapping chosen by its owner. Do not add project-specific meanings to a canonical ID or guess that every local override is the same operation. Private consumer source and operational evidence remain in their authorized private locations.

## Maintenance and publication

```sh
python3 bin/build.py --layout both
python3 bin/ontology.py --write
python3 bin/ontology.py --check
python3 bin/ontology.py --explain host-capability
python3 bin/ontology.py --validate-bindings catalog/ontology-bindings.json
python3 bin/ontology.py --lint docs/design-note.md
```

Change definitions and bindings in the same reviewed PR. Additive terms increment the minor ontology version; editorial clarification increments the patch version; incompatible meanings require a new ID and an explicit migration, with a major version when compatibility breaks. Update the binding version after reviewing that change.

CI validates the registry, opted-in bindings and this generated page. Unregistered interfaces are not claimed as covered. Prose lint is optional and advisory; it does not gate agent tool use.

The repository-backed wiki is reviewable with its source. A separate GitHub Wiki mirror must copy the generated page from an approved source revision, identify that revision, preserve unrelated pages, and avoid hand-editing definitions. If the wiki remote is unavailable, report publication as pending; do not claim this checked-in page is already mirrored.
